question: I'm a CS senior (P-007) in good standing. I want to add a 15-591 (Independent Study, 9 units) to my Spring 2026 schedule, which already includes 15-441 (12 units) and two BA minor courses (~18 units). Does this create an overload problem?

domain_contributions.policies: Students in good standing can overload up to 12 units above normal load with advisor approval. Normal load ≈ 45 units. Any overload requires advisor approval; P-007 is not on AW so independent study is permitted.
domain_contributions.courses: 15-441 (12) + 2 BA courses (~18) + 15-591 (9) = ~39 units total — within normal load; no overload issue

key_facts: P-007 is in good standing — independent study is permitted
Planned load: ~39 units (12 + 18 + 9) = well within normal load threshold of ~45 units
No overload concern; advisor approval for independent study is still needed as a standard process
P-007 took 15-591 in Spring 2025 as well — independent study experience exists
Independent study requires a faculty sponsor and registration
wrong_if_single_domain: Knowing only the policy would suggest independent studies are permitted for good-standing students but cannot confirm the total unit load is acceptable. Knowing only the unit counts cannot determine whether independent study is programmatically permitted for P-007.
common_mistake: Assuming that any addition to the schedule creates an overload without summing the actual unit counts; or assuming independent study is prohibited without checking the student's academic standing
reasoning_chain: Step 1 (programs): P-007 in good standing → independent study permitted
Step 3 (policies): No overload → no special overload approval needed beyond standard IS process
Conclusion: P-007 can add 15-591 without overload concerns; faculty sponsor needed
